chunks: Ismaʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Regarding a pledged item over which the pledger and the pledgee differ, the pledger says, "It is worth such-and-such," and the pledgee says, "It is worth more"; the pledgee is to be believed until the value reaches the price, because he is trustworthy.

key_terms.أَمِينٌ: a trusted custodian whose word carries weight
key_terms.الرَّاهِنُ: the one who gives property in pledge
key_terms.الْمُرْتَهِنُ: the one who takes and holds the pledge as security
key_terms.بِالثَّمَنِ: up to the value or amount of the price/debt in question
key_terms.رَهْنٍ: a pledged item given as collateral for a debt
key_terms.يُصَدَّقُ: is deemed truthful or legally accepted in his claim

ai.seo_question: In a dispute over the value of pledged collateral, whose statement is accepted in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a dispute over the value of collateral in a rahn agreement. Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام states that the pledgee is accepted in his claim up to the amount of the debt, on the basis that he is entrusted with the pledged property.
